system_overview: This specification models a condition-based consensus protocol that uses the maximum proposed value to reach agreement, based on Figure 1 with condition C1 from Mostefaoui et al.'s 2003 paper. The protocol operates in an asynchronous system with crash faults and proceeds in two phases. If a sufficient condition on the input vector holds (enough processes propose the maximum value), the protocol can terminate; otherwise processes deterministically choose from all received values.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes that communicate by message passing. Processes may crash (up to F actual faults, bounded by T maximum tolerated faults), with the constraint that 2T is less than N. Crashed processes stop participating. Each process proposes an initial value from a totally ordered finite set of values.
state_variables: The system tracks: the control location of each process (broadcasting phase 1, waiting for phase 1, preparing, broadcasting phase 2, waiting for phase 2, done, crashed, or choosing), each process's local view of all other processes' values (an N-by-N matrix, initially filled with a special bottom value), each process's proposed value, each process's estimated value (computed as the maximum of its local view after phase 1), each process's decision value (initially bottom), the count of crashed processes, the set of all sent messages, and the set of messages received by each process. Messages carry a type (phase 1 or phase 2), a value, and a sender; phase 2 messages additionally carry an estimated value.
initial_state: Initially, each process is in the broadcast-phase-1 state. Each process has a proposed value drawn from the value set. All local views are filled with the bottom value. All estimated values and decision values are bottom. No processes have crashed. No messages have been sent and no messages have been received.
actions: The protocol operates in two phases: Phase 1: (1) Each process broadcasts a phase-1 message containing its proposed value and moves to the phase-1 waiting state. (2) A process may receive messages, updating its local view with the sender's value when the message type matches the current phase. (3) Once a process in phase-1 waiting has received phase-1 messages from at least N-T distinct senders, it computes its estimated value as the maximum value in its local view, then moves to broadcast phase 2. Phase 2: (4) Each process broadcasts a phase-2 message containing both its proposed value and its estimated value. (5) Once in phase-2 waiting, if a process receives phase-2 messages where at least N-T of them carry the same estimated value, it decides that value and finishes. (6) Alternatively, if a process has received phase-2 messages from all N senders without reaching the N-T threshold for any single estimated value, it moves to a choosing state. (7) In the choosing state, the process deterministically selects a value that appears in its local view and decides it. At any point, a process may crash if fewer than F have crashed so far.
safety_properties: Validity: if a process decides a value, that value was proposed by some process. Agreement: no two processes decide different values.
liveness_properties: Termination: eventually every process either crashes or finishes with a decision. Conditional termination (under Condition C1): if at least F+1 processes propose the maximum value among all proposals, the protocol terminates.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on receiving, broadcasting, phase transitions, and choosing. The specification requires 2T less than N, 0 at most F at most T, and N greater than 0. All values in the value set are distinct from the special bottom value. Condition C1 states that at least F+1 processes must propose the globally maximum value for guaranteed termination.
